item.text:
{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 is reviewed using the supplied EFPA 2025 model, with AI systems replacing human test takers only where explicitly stated below. The evidence supports a bounded interpretation of scores as exact grid-output performance under specified evaluation conditions. It does not establish repeatability, equivalent measurement across AI configurations, or general intelligence. Every numbered descriptive field and rated item is addressed below; no items are intentionally omitted. Section ratings are judgements, not averages, and no aggregate quality score is calculated.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "1: Instrument name and short name: ARC-AGI-2. Developers: ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners; the example figure credits François Chollet and colleagues. Source inspection: 7 October 2026, which is not a publication or review date.",
        "2.1: Content keywords: rule inference, grid problems, reasoning. 2.2: Area: AI benchmarking and reasoning research. 2.3: Intended population: AI systems; eligibility boundaries are not specified. 2.4: Intended users: researchers comparing AI systems, inferred from the stated use.",
        "2.5: One reported problem-averaged performance score; no separate scores established as distinct skills. 2.6: Responses are output grids represented through the evaluation software. 2.8: Verified evaluations specify AI settings, a spending limit and one run; other routes may differ.",
        "2.9: Production-based grid responses scored for exact success. 2.10: Coloured two-dimensional grids. 2.11: 1,000 development problems and three 120-problem evaluation sets; problems may have multiple new inputs. 2.12.1: Individual-system assessment is the applicable interpretation. 2.12.2: Verified testing is controlled automated administration; other routes vary.",
        "2.15: Public, semi-private and private evaluation sets differ in access and were matched for human difficulty; ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions. 2.16: Released problem sets are fixed; no adaptive administration is described. 2.17: The evaluated AI produces the responses; these are performance responses, not psychological self-reports.",
        "3.1: Digital scoring of submitted outputs. 3.2: Up to two attempts per new input; an exact match earns credit, input credits are averaged within each problem, and problem scores are then averaged. 3.3: Raw proportion scores. 3.4: Standard-score transformation is not applicable. 3.5: No differentiated norms are described.",
        "5.1: Available supporting materials include a technical report, public problems, running software, marking tests, evaluation rules and a change record. 5.2: Public digital materials are described. General description: Example-based grid puzzles assess production of exact outputs, with development and evaluation sets separated and hidden-set access controlled.",
        "6.1.1=2: The rule-inference construct and intended task design are explained, although the link to broader intelligence is not established. 6.1.2=2: Human puzzle-solving research informs selection and difficulty; its relevance to AI measurement is limited.",
        "6.1.3.1=2: Example-based grid tasks and exact-answer scoring fit the bounded performance aim. 6.1.3.2=2: Newly written and previously unused puzzles, developer review and removal of repeated rules support content development. 6.1.3.3=2: Human difficulty results and duplicate-rule review inform selection, but final-pool analysis is incomplete.",
        "6.1.6=2: Human-based difficulty assessment and qualitative rule review provide an intelligible item-analysis approach. 6.1.8=2: The rationale and development support grid-task assessment more strongly than broad reasoning claims.",
        "6.2.1=2: The supplied account explains the purpose and task rationale. 6.2.2=2: Sources, selection study and corrections are described, without a complete final-item analysis. 6.2.4=2: Verified settings, spending limits and one-run policy provide some standardisation information.",
        "6.2.6=2: The account clearly identifies the absence of repeated-run precision estimates; this documentation rating does not establish adequate reliability. 6.2.7=2: Content development and human selection research are described. 6.2.10=2: Exposure controls and their limitations are explained.",
        "6.2.11=2: Recorded human background comparisons and evaluation-condition controls provide limited fair-use information. 6.2.13=2: The supplied explanatory language is clear; complete user documentation was not supplied. 6.2.14=2: Documentation explains the bounded task and several limitations, with substantial technical gaps.",
        "6.3.1=2: Verified administration conditions and separation of development from evaluation are described. 6.3.2=2: The software scoring rule and selected marking tests are explained; complete marking verification is absent. 6.3.4=2: The distinction between partial problem credit and fully solving a problem supports interpretation.",
        "6.3.7=2: Restrictions on evaluation-specific adaptation, repeated feedback use and hidden-data handling are described. 6.3.9=2: The account identifies the technical report, rules, software and change record, but supplies limited bibliographic detail. 6.3.10=2: Core procedures are understandable, though operational detail is incomplete. 6.4=2: Rationale and documentation are adequate for a restricted research interpretation.",
        "7.1.2=2: Worked input-output examples make the task understandable at the descriptive level. 7.1.3=2: Examples, development tasks and an exact-output requirement provide basic task instructions.",
        "10.1: Content evidence, evaluated through section 6 as EFPA directs, supports example-based grid-task coverage. Human solvability and duplicate-rule review do not establish comprehensive reasoning coverage.",
        "10.5=2 for bounded grid-output performance: Task content and scoring have a clear relationship to this narrow use. Evidence for broader reasoning, general intelligence or real-world prediction remains insufficient."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "3.2 and 6.3.4: Software awards fractional problem credit, whereas published instructions reserve 'fully solved' for problems with every input correct. Reports must identify which meaning is used.",
        "6.1.3.3 and 6.1.7: The human study used a larger pool than the final benchmark; pooled findings cannot automatically describe final-item quality.",
        "7.1.7=2: Public fixes to coloured squares and unclear examples document material defects and subsequent repair. Their remaining extent is not established. 7.1.8=2: Examples, public materials and corrections support basic material adequacy, while robustness and full item-quality evidence remain unavailable.",
        "8.3.2.1: Corrected problems and code changes can affect score comparability. The change record does not recalculate every affected AI score; no normative distortion is established.",
        "9.4: Human difficulty matching does not demonstrate alternate-form equivalence for AI systems.",
        "10.4: Public evaluation problems permit prior exposure. Hidden-test agreements and monitoring mitigate exposure but acknowledge possible escape; they do not establish absence of contamination.",
        "Final evaluation: Strengths include transparent scoring logic, inspectable public materials, content review and tracked corrections. One-run verified testing, unquantified score variation and unresolved exposure limit comparative conclusions. Under EFPA's critical-attribute guidance, the critical 9.8=0 confines supported use to research or exceptional expert-led interpretation; it does not prove poor repeatability."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1: Review date, previous-review date, local adaptation name and authors, individual original-author list, formal original publisher versus distributor, current-edition publication date, adaptation publication date and original publication date are not supplied. Reviewer identity is an AI benchmark-reviewer perspective, not a claimed human credential.",
        "2.7: Language command, language fluency, reading, writing and digital interaction are reinterpreted as system input/output capabilities; required levels and limitations are not specified. 2.11: Minimum, maximum and typical inputs per problem are absent. 2.13: Required hardware, connectivity and complete runtime arrangements are absent.",
        "2.14: Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and feedback times are not supplied. Automated components are described, but complete automation of each administrator function is not established, so zero times are not assumed.",
        "4.1: Availability and number of distinct digitally generated report products are not established. 4.2: Numerical outputs, costs, times and problem scores are reportedly released. 4.3: Their complete static, interactive or multimedia format is unknown. 4.4: Problem-level and overall score structure is described, but interpretive report structure is not.",
        "4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10: Report contextual tailoring, development, modifiability, score-to-text transparency, interpretive content and intended recipient categories are not established. Publication of numerical outputs alone does not answer these fields.",
        "5.3: Supplier-required qualifications are unspecified; this is not evidence that none are required.",
        "6.1.5: Psychometric framework is not specified. Human difficulty information is described, but no final-item difficulty table, item means/SDs, item-total correlations, IRT parameters, distractor statistics or DIF results are supplied. 6.1.7=0: Final-pool discrimination, difficulty spread, variability and ceiling/floor results are insufficiently presented.",
        "6.2.8=0: No internal-structure evidence is described. 6.2.9=0: No adequate account of relationships with other construct markers or external criteria is supplied. 6.2.12=0: Report format, precision and interpretive validity are insufficiently documented.",
        "6.3.5=0: Stakeholder feedback procedures are not detailed. 6.3.6=0: Guidance connecting subgroup differences or possible bias to fair AI comparisons is insufficient. 6.3.8=0: Complete hardware/software requirements, error handling and technical support arrangements are absent.",
        "7.1.1=0: Selected marking tests do not establish general software robustness. 7.1.4=0: Submission ease and error handling are insufficiently documented. 7.1.5=0: The evaluation interface was not supplied for assessment.",
        "9.1: No reliability coefficients or standard errors for the score or relevant AI groups are supplied. 9.3.1=0, 9.3.2=0: Repeated-run sample sizes and coefficients are absent. 9.3.3: Retest interval is unreported. 9.3.4: No repeated-run sample is described, so matching to intended systems cannot be judged.",
        "9.4.1=0, 9.4.2=0: AI alternate-form study sizes and coefficients are absent. 9.4.3: Matching of equivalence-study systems to intended systems is unknown.",
        "9.7.1=0, 9.7.3=0: No alternative precision-study sample or results are supplied. 9.7.2: No alternative precision method is established; one verified run is not a precision estimate. 9.8=0, critical: Score repeatability and uncertainty remain unquantified.",
        "10.2.1: No factor analysis, invariance analysis or other dimensionality method is reported. 10.2.2=0, 10.2.3=0: Dimensional structure and equivalence across relevant AI groups are unestablished.",
        "10.3.1.1: Background-factor comparisons are reported for human puzzle solvers, not AI construct validation. 10.3.1.2=0: No adequately specified AI known-group validation hypotheses and results are supplied.",
        "10.3.1.3=0, 10.3.1.4=0: No convergent or discriminant correlations, marker reliability information or method-effect analyses are supplied. 10.3.1.6=0: No systematic manipulation study of AI instructions, presentation or software is supplied.",
        "10.3.1.7=0: Other AI construct-validation evidence is not established. 10.3.1.8=0: Relevant AI validation sample sizes are absent. 10.3.1.9=0: Suitable marker quality is unreported. 10.3.1.10: Validation-study ages cannot be established. 10.3.1.11=0: Relationships with other variables do not substantiate the broader claims.",
        "10.3.2.1: No predictive, concurrent or postdictive external-criterion study is supplied. 10.3.2.2=0, 10.3.2.3=0, 10.3.2.4=0: Relevant study sizes, criterion quality and criterion relationships are absent. 10.3.2.6: Criterion-study ages are unknown. 10.3.2.7=0: Prediction of language, social or real-world performance is unresolved.",
        "10.4.1: Other evidence concerns intended response processes and preventing exposure or shortcut-based success. 10.4.2=0, 10.4.3=0: No sufficient study establishes that intended reasoning produces the scores or excludes unintended successful routes.",
        "11.1.1=0, 11.1.2=0: Construct applicability across relevant AI groups and corresponding comparison guidance are insufficiently established. 11.2=0: Inclusive design across relevant system interfaces and groups is not demonstrated.",
        "11.3=0: Human background findings do not supply AI subgroup piloting or DIF evidence. 11.4=0: Comparable subgroup precision is unreported. 11.5=0: Equivalent score meaning and criterion relationships across AI groups are unreported.",
        "11.7=0: Complete score reports and guidance about potential comparison bias are unavailable. 11.8=0: Evidence supporting fair use across relevant AI comparison conditions is insufficient; unfairness is not thereby established.",
        "12.1=0, 12.2=0, 12.3=0, 12.4=0, 12.5=0, 12.6=0, 12.7=0: Under the score-report reinterpretation, scope, interpretation consistency, validity, freedom from bias, acceptability, detail and overall quality cannot be judged. Three actual reports with differing score profiles, as EFPA requests, are not supplied; the complete release archive was not checked."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Scope: EFPA's human psychological-testing model is applied to an AI benchmark by explicit analogy. This is not an EFPA endorsement. Supplied passages are the sole evidence; referenced originals were not independently inspected.",
        "2.7: Human attention, handedness, hearing, motor capabilities and vision are inapplicable as human attributes. Grid-input processing is relevant, but human sensory prerequisites cannot be assigned to the AI. Language and digital requirements are treated as system-interface requirements.",
        "6.1.4=n/a, 6.2.3=n/a: No translated or locally adapted benchmark version is identified. Applying EFPA to AI is a review adaptation, not evidence of a translated test.",
        "6.2.5=n/a, 6.3.3=n/a: No norm conversion is used in the bounded raw-score comparison. Norm documentation and norm-selection instructions therefore have no demonstrated role.",
        "6.3.5: Human emotional debriefing is inapplicable; communication of findings to researchers remains relevant and is rated separately.",
        "7.1.6=n/a: Human disability accessibility for AI test takers is inapplicable. Compatibility across AI input interfaces remains relevant under materials and fair-use review.",
        "7.2.1=n/a, 7.2.2=n/a, 7.2.3=n/a, 7.2.4=n/a, 7.2.5=n/a, 7.2.6=n/a, 7.2.7=n/a: No paper-and-pencil or other non-digital administration is described.",
        "8.1.1=n/a, 8.1.2=n/a, 8.1.3.1=n/a, 8.1.3.2=n/a, 8.1.3.3=n/a: No population-norm interpretation, classical norming or continuous norming is claimed for the bounded comparison. 8.1.4: No norm-sample selection procedure applies. The 407 people and 515 sessions concern puzzle selection, not AI norms.",
        "8.2.1.1=n/a, 8.2.1.2=n/a, 8.2.1.5=n/a: No expert-set critical performance score is described. 8.2.1.3 and 8.2.1.4: No standard-setting or corresponding agreement method applies. 8.2.2=n/a: No empirically derived critical score is described. Exact-answer item marking is not standard setting.",
        "8.3.1=n/a, 8.3.2.1=n/a as norm ratings, 8.3.3=n/a: Norm age and adequacy do not apply to the restricted raw-score comparison. 8.3.2.2: This uses EFPA's exception only for bounded score comparison; wider population or mastery interpretations are unsupported. 8.3.2.3: No norm-based fair-use information is established.",
        "9.2.1=n/a, 9.2.2=n/a, 9.2.3=n/a, 9.2.4=n/a: For the described heterogeneous puzzle aggregate, internal consistency is not selected as an appropriate precision method under EFPA's guidance. This does not remove the requirement for repeated-run, equivalent-form or alternative precision evidence.",
        "9.3: Retesting means repeated evaluation of a fixed AI configuration; version changes must not be treated automatically as measurement error. 9.4: Equivalence means comparable AI measurement across evaluation sets, beyond matched human difficulty.",
        "9.5.1=n/a, 9.5.2=n/a, 9.5.3=n/a: No IRT-based scoring or precision method is described.",
        "9.6.1=n/a, 9.6.2=n/a, 9.6.3=n/a: Exact grid comparison uses no judgemental response scoring. Software correctness remains relevant; human puzzle reviewers are not response scorers.",
        "10.3.1.5=n/a: No MTMM validation design is identified. 10.3.2.5=n/a: No diagnostic classification or qualitative external criterion is claimed; exact-answer accuracy is not diagnostic criterion validity.",
        "11: Human demographic fairness is not inferred for AI systems. Relevant analogies concern system groups, exposure, access and administration conditions; human background findings cannot establish AI measurement fairness.",
        "11.6.1=n/a, 11.6.2=n/a: Neither population-norm interpretation nor critical-score classification is described.",
        "4 and 12: Numerical evaluation outputs are treated provisionally as score reports. This does not establish that separate automated interpretive report products exist.",
        "Summary of ratings: 6.4=2; 7.1.8=2; 7.2.7=n/a; 8.3.3=n/a; 9.8=0, critical; 10.5=2 for bounded grid performance; 11.8=0; 12.7=0. The summary table's reference to 7.2.8 conflicts with the supplied section's 7.2.7; no separate 7.2.8 item is provided.",
        "Final conclusions: Use for exploratory comparisons of exact grid-output performance with explicit version, exposure and run conditions. Skilled benchmark and measurement interpretation is needed; supplier qualification requirements are unknown.",
        "Part C: Evidence consists solely of the supplied ARC-AGI-2 passages and supplied EFPA model. Attribution: European Federation of Psychologists' Associations AISBL, 2025, version 5.0, https://www.efpa.eu/, CC BY-SA 4.0. This explicitly adapted application retains that attribution and ShareAlike licence; no referenced external bibliography was consulted."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Unclear examples have required corrections, and 'fully solved' differs from fractional software credit. Effects of instruction and presentation changes on AI scores remain untested in the supplied evidence."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA is reviewed using the supplied EFPA 2025 model, with explicit AI-specific reinterpretations. Its scores describe performance on six Formula SAE task groups under particular information-supply and marking conditions. Real engineering materials support relevance, but documented scoring sensitivities and restricted coverage weaken claims of engineering understanding or fine system rankings. Every numbered descriptive field and rated item is addressed below; no items are intentionally omitted. Section ratings are judgements, not averages, and no aggregate quality score is calculated.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "1: Instrument name and short name: DesignQA. Version: original benchmark described in the 2024 paper, together with public scoring software. Developers: researchers and engineers. Sources inspected on 6 October 2026; this is not the review date or a software-version identifier.",
        "2.1: Content keywords: rule retrieval, engineering-document interpretation, design assessment. 2.2: Area: AI benchmarking with engineering materials. 2.3: Intended population: AI systems. 2.4: Intended users: researchers comparing systems, inferred from the stated use.",
        "2.5: Six task-group scores plus a software overall score: individual-rule retrieval, related-rule retrieval, technical-term explanation, component presence, dimensional checking and performance assessment. These are task categories, not established distinct latent skills.",
        "2.6: Text responses through the evaluation system. 2.8: Information supply varies between complete rulebooks and retrieved passages; settings and instructions are described in the paper. 2.9: Open text and yes/no responses, sometimes with explanations. 2.10: Text rules, vehicle images and drawings.",
        "2.11: 1,451 question-answer pairs; 1,192 individual-rule questions and 16 performance questions. Other group counts are not supplied. 2.12.1: Individual-system assessment. 2.12.2: Researcher-configured automated administration; no uniform supervision category is established.",
        "2.15: Experiments vary supplied passages, labels, scale bars and highlighting; these are not established equivalent forms. 2.16: A fixed released question collection is described, without adaptive item selection. 2.17: Evaluated AIs produce task responses, not psychological self-reports.",
        "3.1: Digital scoring of AI responses. 3.2: Task-dependent text similarity and yes/no correctness, with some explanation scoring; the overall score weights each task group equally. 3.3: Raw task metrics and their composite. 3.4: Standard-score transformation is not applicable. 3.5: No differentiated norms are described.",
        "5.1: Public questions, instructions, scoring code, some AI responses and the paper provide supporting materials. 5.2: Public digital publication. General description: DesignQA uses Formula SAE rules and vehicle materials to test retrieval, interpretation and application through six unevenly sized task groups.",
        "6.1.1=2: Engineering-document understanding is linked to identifiable task types. 6.1.3.2=2: Real rules, vehicle designs, test data and practitioner contributions support content relevance.",
        "6.2.1=2: The task rationale is understandable. 6.2.2=2: Sources and manual review procedures are described, including exceptions. 6.2.4=2: Instructions, settings and differing information supply are described, though historical reproducibility is incomplete.",
        "6.2.7=2: Content sources and reviewer checking are explained. 6.2.10=2: Passage, image and formatting influences are discussed. 6.2.13=2: The supplied account is clear; the full documentation was not provided. 6.2.14=2: Documentation identifies the tasks, scoring methods and several limitations, while important technical information is missing.",
        "6.3.1=2: The paper describes main instructions and settings, with incomplete links to exact historical runs. 6.3.2=2: Marking methods are described and some test files exist; adequate description does not establish adequate marking validity.",
        "6.3.4=2: Acknowledged limits on document transfer and imperfect marking support cautious interpretation. 6.3.9=2: The paper and public materials are identified, although full bibliographic and result-specific references are absent. 6.3.10=2: Basic research procedures are described, with material reproducibility and reuse gaps.",
        "7.1.2=2: Named task categories and response types give an understandable task outline. 7.1.3=2: Instructions are available and experimental input manipulations are described, but complete practice and error-handling guidance is not established.",
        "10.1: As EFPA directs, content evidence is considered through section 6. Actual competition rules and vehicle materials support task relevance; they do not establish representative coverage of engineering work.",
        "10.3.1.1: Other-model and random-guessing comparisons, plus input manipulations, are described. 10.3.1.6=2: Passage, dimension-label, scale-bar and highlighting manipulations provide useful evidence about condition sensitivity, without establishing broad construct validity.",
        "10.4.1: Other evidence concerns response processes and unintended routes to credit. The all-compliant scale-bar portion identifies a concrete alternative route to yes/no credit; no tested AI is shown to have used it."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "6.1.3.1=1: Equal weighting combines very different group sizes and marking methods without evidence that the composite measures a coherent engineering-understanding construct.",
        "6.1.3.3=1: Manual checking has exceptions and explanation checks can be limited to supporting the yes/no answer. The all-compliant scale-bar portion leaves a documented non-understanding route to credit. Final selection does not adequately address this problem.",
        "6.1.8=1: Practical content sources are a strength, but selection and scoring design do not adequately support the breadth of the intended understanding claim. 6.4=1: Clear documentation cannot compensate for the documented design problems affecting the proposed score interpretation.",
        "7.1.7=1: The all-compliant scale-bar portion permits constant 'yes' responses to earn decision credit, weakening item quality for design-rule assessment. 7.1.8=1: This demonstrated content problem limits material adequacy for the intended measurement use.",
        "3.2 and 6.3.2: Missing commas and valid related rules absent from reference answers can affect credit. These are documented scoring sensitivities, not merely hypothetical errors.",
        "2.8 and 10.3.1: Systems receive different information, so comparisons concern each AI together with its information supply. They do not isolate AI capability under identical inputs.",
        "2.11 and 9.7: In the 16-question performance group, one additional correct answer changes accuracy by 6.25 percentage points. This limits score resolution; it is not itself a reliability coefficient.",
        "5.1 and 6.2.4: Historical software, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every reported result, and one answer file has fewer rows than the paper's corresponding question count.",
        "8.3.2.1: Software revisions are identifiable but their score effects lack a clear change record. This is a score-version comparability concern; normative distortion is not established.",
        "10.4.3=1: Documented wording sensitivity and the constant-answer opportunity undermine an exclusive interpretation of credit as engineering understanding. Their effects across the complete benchmark are not quantified.",
        "10.5=1, critical for engineering-understanding claims: Content relevance provides some support, but known scoring and shortcut problems weaken the claimed interpretation. Transfer to other technical documents and projects remains unestablished.",
        "Final evaluation: Strengths include authentic materials, six explicit task types, public inspection opportunities and informative input manipulations. Known marking sensitivities, unequal information supply, restricted coverage and incomplete precision evidence limit engineering-competence claims and close rankings. Critical 9.8=0 and 10.5=1 invoke EFPA's recommendation for research or exceptional expert-led use."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1: Review date, previous-review date, local adaptation name and authors, individual original-author list, formal publisher/distributor details, exact current software edition and publication date, adaptation date and exact original publication date are not supplied. The original paper's year is 2024. Reviewer identity is an AI benchmark-reviewer perspective, not a claimed human credential.",
        "2.7: Required levels of language command, fluency, reading, writing and digital interaction are not specified as system capabilities. 2.13: Complete hardware, connectivity and runtime requirements are absent.",
        "2.14: Preparation, administration, scoring, analysis and stakeholder-feedback times are not supplied. Described automation does not establish that every administrator function requires zero time.",
        "4.1: Distinct digitally generated report products and their number are not established. 4.2: The paper contains system results and the software produces group and overall scores. 4.3: Complete report presentation formats are unknown. 4.4: Task-group and composite score structure is known, but interpretive report structure is not.",
        "4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10: Context tailoring, report-content development, modifiability, score-to-text mapping, interpretive content and intended recipient categories are not established. Numerical outputs alone do not answer these fields.",
        "5.3: Supplier-required qualifications are unspecified. A licence file and complete responsible-reuse rules were not found in the inspected sources; this does not establish that permission is unavailable or reuse prohibited.",
        "6.1.2=0: A sufficient empirical research summary grounding the intended construct is not supplied. 6.1.5: Psychometric framework is unspecified; no item-level difficulty, mean/SD, item-total, IRT, distractor or DIF statistics are supplied.",
        "6.1.6=0: Manual checking and aggregate experimental results do not establish a systematic psychometric item-analysis methodology. 6.1.7=0: Item discrimination, difficulty distributions and ceiling/floor results are insufficiently presented; the known shortcut problem does not supply those missing statistics.",
        "6.2.6=0: Reliability and precision methods and results are insufficiently documented. 6.2.8=0: Internal-structure evidence is absent. 6.2.9=0: A sufficient account of convergent, discriminant or external-criterion validation is absent.",
        "6.2.11=0: Guidance for fair comparisons across relevant system and administration groups is insufficient. 6.2.12=0: Report precision, validity and audience suitability are not documented.",
        "6.3.5=0: Stakeholder-feedback procedures are not supplied. 6.3.6=0: Guidance for identifying and addressing comparison bias is insufficient. 6.3.7=0: Clear restrictions on training exposure, repeated submissions and appropriate populations are unavailable. 6.3.8=0: Complete operational requirements, error handling and technical-support arrangements are absent.",
        "7.1.1=0: Small marking-test files do not establish software robustness. 7.1.4=0: Response-entry ease and error handling are unestablished. 7.1.5=0: Interface quality cannot be judged from the supplied account.",
        "9.1: No established reliability coefficients or standard errors for the six groups, composite or relevant system groups are supplied. 9.2.1=0, 9.2.3=0: Suitable internal-consistency samples and coefficients are unavailable where that method might fit a particular group. 9.2.2: No coefficients are identified. 9.2.4: Matching of any such sample to intended systems is unknown.",
        "9.3.1=0, 9.3.2=0: Identical-condition retest study sizes and coefficients are absent. 9.3.3: Retest interval is unreported. 9.3.4: No suitable retest sample is described. Five different passage sets do not isolate identical-condition repeatability.",
        "9.6.1=0, 9.6.3=0: Where reference answers or explanations depend on reviewer judgement, sufficient comparison studies and agreement coefficients are absent. 9.6.2: No agreement statistic is reported. Two additional reviewers do not establish agreement magnitude or residual error rates.",
        "9.7.1=0, 9.7.3=0: No adequately documented alternative precision sample or results are supplied. 9.7.2: Variation across five passage sets is condition sensitivity, not an isolated repeatability estimate. 9.8=0, critical: Evidence is insufficient to quantify score uncertainty or support small system differences.",
        "10.2.1: No dimensionality, invariance or DIF technique is reported. 10.2.2=0, 10.2.3=0: Neither six distinct skills nor a coherent composite structure, nor equivalence across relevant groups, is established.",
        "10.3.1.2=0: Named AI comparisons and random guessing do not supply sufficiently justified known-group validation. 10.3.1.3=0, 10.3.1.4=0: Convergent and discriminant correlations, marker precision and method-effect analyses are absent.",
        "10.3.1.7=0: No additional adequate relation-based validation is established. 10.3.1.8=0: Suitable validation-study sample sizes are not supplied; question counts are not automatically counts of independent systems or validation observations.",
        "10.3.1.9=0: Relevant marker quality is unestablished, and no human-engineer baseline is reported. 10.3.1.10: The paper is from 2024, but validation data-collection dates are not supplied. 10.3.1.11=0: Manipulations and model comparisons do not sufficiently establish intended convergent and discriminant relationships.",
        "10.3.2.1: No predictive, concurrent or postdictive external engineering-outcome study is identified. 10.3.2.2=0, 10.3.2.3=0, 10.3.2.4=0: Relevant sample sizes, external-criterion quality and criterion relationships are absent.",
        "10.3.2.6: Criterion-study ages are unknown. 10.3.2.7=0: Prediction of performance on other documents or actual engineering projects is unestablished. Benchmark marking accuracy is not itself evidence of this transfer.",
        "10.4.2=0: Systematic study of unintended strategies, contamination and response processes is insufficient. Public questions and rulebook, possible similar-image exposure and unverified training histories leave prior exposure unresolved.",
